findings.title: Client-visibility filtering is bypassed on comments/timeline side-channel endpoints
findings.evidence: Re-verified at main@3fa9f636 (read-only). Each nested comments/timeline route now (a) loads the parent with its visibility column and 404s when the parent is not client-visible, then (b) filters module_comments to is_internal=false for client members: approvals.ts:465 and :539 (parent check), :475 (is_internal); assets.ts:361 and :430, :371; findings.ts:464 and :536, :473; proposals.ts:1015 and :1089, :1025. The detail endpoints keep the same predicate (approvals.ts:189, assets.ts:162, findings.ts:164, proposals.ts:145). Regression coverage: apps/api/src/__tests__/client-visibility-sidechannels.test.ts:145-200 (internal parent -> 404 across each path; client-visible parent -> comments query gets .eq('is_internal', false)). Not executed here (node_modules absent); code and tests are present at this commit. Residual (not a re-open): module_timeline_events rows are still returned for a client-visible parent because that table has no per-event internal flag; only status/workflow events are written there.
findings.remediation: No action required for the finding. Optional follow-up: add an is_internal/visibility column to module_timeline_events if any timeline event may ever carry internal-only text.

findings.title: File-request upload listing and signed URLs skip the parent request's visibility check
findings.evidence: Re-verified at main@3fa9f636: apps/api/src/routes/file-requests.ts:407 (GET /:id/uploads) and :444 (GET /:id/uploads/:uploadId/signed-url) both load the parent request's visibility and call isClientVisible before listing or signing; the signed-URL route also keeps the upload row bound to request.id and the resolved org (:452-458). The detail endpoint keeps the same rule (:380). Both routes now also carry requirePermission('file-requests','view') (:394, :421). Regression tests: apps/api/src/__tests__/file-requests.test.ts:477-524 (internal parent hides uploads and signed URLs; client-visible parent still lists).

findings.title: Client roles granted ai:view can read every AI draft output in the organization
findings.evidence: Re-verified at main@3fa9f636: apps/api/src/routes/ai.ts:31-35 adds assertInternalDraftReader (isClientMember -> 403) and it is awaited in GET /ai/drafts (:555) and GET /ai/drafts/:id (:581); the review/write routes keep ai:edit/create gates (:531, :596). The ai:view grant to client roles is unchanged and intentional (supabase/migrations/5302463_client_portal_ai_and_visibility.sql:22-33). Regression tests: apps/api/src/__tests__/ai.test.ts:236-253 (client role denied on list and detail). The separate triage-draft surface is covered as SEC-P3-016.

findings.title: Client-visibility helper fails open and exempts API-key requests
findings.evidence: Re-verified at main@3fa9f636. Fail-open half is fixed: apps/api/src/lib/client-visibility.ts:100 throws on the membership query error (previously swallowed) and :107-110 now sets result=true (client-scoped / visibility filter applied) instead of the staff view, logging the regression. The second half is unchanged: :85-92 still returns false (staff view) for any req.apiKey request. The exemption is now documented as a system/integration path (:81-88) and is bounded today because api-keys:manage is an admin-scope permission (supabase/migrations/5302118_permission_matrix_full_catalog.sql:306-307) and the client-role grant loop only grants scope in ('portal','both') (:407-413), so client roles cannot mint keys; the route is also permission-gated (apps/api/src/routes/api-keys.ts:65). It remains a latent bypass if a client-scoped key or a custom role with api-keys:manage is ever introduced.
findings.remediation: Replace the blanket req.apiKey -> staff-view return with the key's own role/tenant scope (e.g. resolve the key creator's membership or store a client/system flag on api_keys), and add a test that a client-capable key cannot see internal rows. Until then, keep api-keys:* out of every client/custom role.

findings.title: GET /ai/triage is the only AI route without an ai:view gate
findings.evidence: Re-verified at main@3fa9f636: apps/api/src/routes/ai.ts:336 now mounts requirePermission('ai','view') on GET /ai/triage, matching the other AI reads (:364, :553, :579). The route is therefore reached only by callers holding ai:view (which includes client roles by design; see SEC-P3-016 for the data-scope consequence).
findings.remediation: No action required for the missing gate itself.

findings.title: A cross-tenant admin membership widens admin scope to orgs where the user is only a client/member
findings.evidence: Re-verified at main@3fa9f636: apps/api/src/lib/admin-scope.ts:66-95 now derives adminOrgIds only from rows whose role key is cross-tenant and, for a non-super-admin admin, confines the scope to the request-pinned org or adminOrgIds (never every membership); allTenants still requires the profiles.is_super_admin flag AND a cross-tenant role (:76-82). apps/api/src/middleware/org-access.ts:143-162 pins an unpinned tenant admin to adminMemberships[0] and only treats a super-admin profile with an admin membership as org-agnostic; otherwise it pins to the admin org (:153-162). apps/api/src/middleware/admin.ts:49-58 rejects an explicit org unless the caller is super_admin or admin in that org. routes/search.ts:78-97 uses the same adminOrgIds set. Regression tests: apps/api/src/__tests__/admin-scope-cross-org.test.ts:38-117, apps/api/src/__tests__/middleware-org-access.test.ts:353, apps/api/src/__tests__/search-tenant-scope.test.ts:191. The non-admin branch intentionally still returns all approved orgs (:97-99) so client exports keep working; it is only reachable behind requireAdmin for admin surfaces.

findings.title: Module read endpoints are org-scoped but not permission-gated (catalog view grants are UI-only)
findings.evidence: Re-verified at main@3fa9f636: every primary module read now carries requirePermission(module,'view'): assets.ts:44/75/108/143, approvals.ts:52/95/122/165, findings.ts:51/84/118/143, proposals.ts:48/81/111, qbr.ts:22/47, service-catalog.ts:20/43, file-requests.ts:343/370 (and :394/:421 nested), domain-monitors.ts:41/70/100/157, vendors.ts:29/62 and :183. Vendor contracts are no longer served under the admin-only 'vendors' module: the routes use the client-scope 'vendor-contracts'/'vendor-contacts' permissions (supabase/migrations/5302118:260-267) and still apply client visibility (vendors.ts:47, :74). Regression coverage was extended in the #335 batch (client-visibility-sidechannels.test.ts, file-requests.test.ts).

findings.title: notifications INSERT policy allows any authenticated user to write a self-addressed row into an arbitrary organization
findings.evidence: Re-verified at main@3fa9f636: supabase/migrations/5302466_notifications_insert_membership_scope.sql:19-36 recreates notifications_insert_system_or_admin so the self branch requires user_id = auth.uid() AND (organization_id is null OR public.is_org_member(organization_id)); the admin/platform branch is unchanged. is_org_member filters status='approved' (supabase/migrations/5302100_fix_rls_membership_status.sql:14-19) and its search_path is pinned (supabase/migrations/5302112_fix_rls_approved_membership.sql:20). node scripts/verify-rls.mjs reports 140/140 tables RLS-enabled, 1,036 policies, 0 failures / 0 warnings at this commit. Migration is wrapped in begin/commit and covered by apps/api/src/__tests__/rls-policy-fix-migrations.test.ts:164-178.

findings.title: Direct anon INSERT on store_quotes bypasses the consent gate, validation and rate limits
findings.evidence: Re-verified at main@3fa9f636: supabase/migrations/5302465_revoke_anon_store_quotes_insert.sql:16-17 drops policy anon_insert_quotes and revokes INSERT from anon. The only INSERT grant to anon was supabase/migrations/5302434_anon_privilege_least_privilege.sql:74 (earlier version), which this migration now removes; no later migration re-grants store_quotes write access (grep of supabase/migrations shows 5302465 as the last file touching the table). The authenticated path keeps its approved-membership predicate (5302448:19-23) and POST /store/quotes remains the consent-enforcing write path (:17-21 of 5302449). Covered by apps/api/src/__tests__/rls-policy-fix-migrations.test.ts:140-162.

findings.title: Proposal client decisions can be recorded or overwritten by internal staff (no client-role or immutability check)
findings.evidence: Re-verified at main@3fa9f636: apps/api/src/routes/proposals.ts:813-823 now requires the proposal to be approved and published/client-visible; :825-830 rejects any caller that is not a client member (isClientMember -> 403); :832-835 returns 409 when metadata.clientDecision already exists, so a second caller cannot flip it. The new audited reset path is staff-only and org-scoped via router-level requireOrgAccess + loadOwned (proposals.ts:886-912). Tests: apps/api/src/__tests__/proposals.test.ts:368-401 (staff rejected, client allowed once, overwrite refused).

findings.title: NEW: client roles can still read internal comments on tickets and project tasks (is_internal is not enforced on the API or the RLS policy)
findings.evidence: NEW at main@3fa9f636, discovered while re-verifying SEC-P1-011; the defect predates the delta but is in the same class and was not covered by the Nov 3 finding. (1) GET /tickets/:id embeds every comment row with `.select("*, ticket_comments(*)")` without an is_internal predicate (apps/api/src/routes/tickets.ts:143); GET /tickets/:id/comments returns all rows with only a ticket-org check (tickets.ts:356-378, query at :369-373); neither route carries requirePermission('tickets','view') or an isClientMember filter. (2) GET /projects/:id/tasks/comments applies `.eq('is_internal', false)` only when the caller voluntarily passes ?is_internal=false (apps/api/src/routes/projects.ts:845-847); omitting the parameter returns internal notes, and the route has no permission/client gate (:830-851). Client roles hold tickets:view and projects:view (catalog scope 'both', supabase/migrations/5302118_permission_matrix_full_catalog.sql:30,38; client_admin/client_user grant loop at :407-430), and the mct_session cookie is scoped to the parent domain so a client can call the API directly. Intent is unambiguous: the portal UI filters internal rows client-side (apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/support/[ticketId]/page.tsx:172) and the admin ticket form has an 'Internal only' checkbox (apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/tickets/[ticketId]/page.tsx:562). The DB is not a second line of defence: the ticket_comments SELECT policy is org-membership only (supabase/migrations/5302026_supabase_consolidated_fresh_bootstrap_20260529.corrected.v3.sql:1188-1195). Secondary: POST /tickets/:id/comments accepts isInternal from any caller with tickets:edit (tickets.ts:398-405), so a client_admin can also forge an internal-only note.
findings.remediation: Add a client-aware gate to the ticket and project-task comment reads: require tickets:view / projects:view, and when isClientMember(req) add `.eq('is_internal', false)` (also replace the embedded ticket_comments(*) select with an explicit filtered sub-select, or drop it from GET /tickets/:id and keep the dedicated comments endpoint). Force is_internal=false (or 403) for client callers on the comment POST routes. Add an `is_internal = false OR is_staff(organization_id)` predicate to the ticket_comments/project_task_comments SELECT RLS policies as defence in depth. Regression tests: a client token must not see an is_internal=true row via either route or via the embedded detail payload.

findings.title: NEW: GET /ai/triage returns every triage draft in the org (raw descriptions and first-response drafts) to client roles holding ai:view
findings.evidence: NEW at main@3fa9f636. supabase/migrations/5302463_client_portal_ai_and_visibility.sql:22-33 grants ai:view to client_admin/client_user/client-viewer/client-billing by design. GET /ai/triage (apps/api/src/routes/ai.ts:336-357) lists ticket_triage_drafts for the injected organization with no created_by, status or per-client filter, and the table has no visibility column (supabase/migrations/5302065_ticket_triage.sql:4-21). The portal AI Triage page renders the same rows, including raw_description and suggested fields, for any approved membership (apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/ai-triage/page.tsx:27-60), which contradicts the documented contract 'Client: triage analysis + copilot on own tickets' (docs/modules/ai-tools.md:44). ai_draft_outputs is correctly staff-only (SEC-P2-020), so this is the remaining member of the same AI-output surface. Impact is bounded to the client's own tenant (the rows are for that org's tickets), hence P3 rather than P2.
findings.remediation: For client members, filter the list to `created_by = req.authUser.userId` (or add a visibility/client_id column and filter on it), or move the client surface to a dedicated GET /ai/triage/mine endpoint and keep GET /ai/triage staff-only. Add a test that a client token only sees triage drafts it created.

findings.title: NEW: SSO callback forwards the caller's entire cookie jar (including mct_session and csrf_token) to the API when only the PKCE verifier is needed
findings.evidence: NEW at main@3fa9f636 (SSO feature, commits 9d2311e2/306b0ff8). apps/web/app/auth/callback/route.ts:24-27 posts `cookies: request.headers.get("cookie") || ""` to /api/v1/auth/callback. The API uses that blob only to extract the `sb-<ref>-auth-token-code-verifier` cookie (apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts:223-229, :249-253); it never needs mct_session, csrf_token or mct_active_org. The session JWT therefore crosses the web->API service boundary inside a JSON body on every login/reset callback. No concrete sink was found at this commit (the API request logger and error handler do not log request bodies, apps/api/src/middleware/request-id.ts, middleware/error.ts:46-52, and Sentry runs beforeSend=scrubSentryEvent with sendDefaultPii=false, apps/api/src/lib/sentry.ts:16-17), so this is least-privilege hygiene, not a proven leak.
findings.remediation: Parse the Cookie header in the web route and forward only the `sb-<ref>-auth-token-code-verifier` value (or accept a dedicated `code_verifier` field, which the API already supports at auth.ts:234-250). Do not put mct_session/csrf_token in the request body.

findings.title: NEW: the SSO PKCE start route and the verifier-missing/negative callback paths have no regression tests
findings.evidence: NEW at main@3fa9f636. apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts:796-824 (/auth/sso) has no test: grep for 'sso' under apps/api/src/__tests__ and apps/web/__tests__ returns no test for the route or for ssoLoginAction. The added callback suite (apps/api/src/__tests__/auth.test.ts:603-655) covers only the happy path (grant_type=pkce + verifier cookie), a generic 401 on a failed exchange, and the required-auth_code 400; it never asserts that a missing or mismatched code_verifier is rejected, so a future change that drops PKCE binding (e.g. exchanging without the verifier) would not fail CI. No test covers apps/web/lib/auth/auth-actions.ts:45-64 setting the verifier cookie before redirecting.
findings.remediation: Add tests for: missing verifier + valid-looking code -> 401 and no access token; mismatched verifier -> 401; /auth/sso returns redirect_to = `${APP_BASE_URL}/auth/callback`, code_challenge_method=S256 and a cookieName derived from SUPABASE_URL; ssoLoginAction sets the cookie with httpOnly and maxAge before redirect. This is an assurance gap, not an exploitable defect.
